sections.heading: Similar solids and scale factor in 3D

questions.q: Two similar cylinders have a scale factor of $\dfrac{2}{3}$. If the smaller cylinder has volume 40, find the volume of the larger cylinder.
questions.answer: Volumes of similar solids scale by the CUBE of the linear scale factor: $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^3=\dfrac{27}{8}$. Larger volume: $40\times\dfrac{27}{8}=135$.

questions.q: A solid consists of a cylinder of radius 3 and height 8, topped with a hemisphere of the same radius. Find the total volume, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Cylinder volume: $\pi r^2h=\pi(9)(8)=72\pi$. Hemisphere volume: $\dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi(27)=18\pi$. Total volume: $72\pi+18\pi=90\pi$.

This question has two parts. A circle has radius 10. A chord is drawn 6 units from the center. (a) Find the length of the chord, using the relationship between the radius, the distance from center to chord, and half the chord length (a right triangle relationship). (b) Find the area of the minor segment cut off by this chord, to the nearest whole number, given that the central angle subtended by the chord is approximately $106.3^\circ$ and $\sin(106.3^\circ)\approx0.960$.
questions.answer: (a) Half the chord length: $\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=\sqrt{64}=8$. Full chord length: $16$. (b) Segment area = sector area − triangle area. Sector area: $\dfrac{106.3}{360}\times\pi(10)^2\approx0.2953\times314.16\approx92.8$. Triangle area: $\dfrac{1}{2}(10)(10)\sin(106.3^\circ)\approx50(0.960)=48$. Segment area: $92.8-48\approx45$.

sections.heading: The 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles in composite figures

questions.q: An equilateral triangle has side length 10. Find its height and area, using the fact that the height splits it into two 30-60-90 triangles.
questions.answer: The height corresponds to the longer leg of a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse 10 and shorter leg 5: height $=5\sqrt{3}$. Area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(10)(5\sqrt{3})=25\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 5. Find the side length of the square, using the fact that the diagonal of the square equals the diameter of the circle.
questions.answer: Diameter $=2(5)=10$. For a square, diagonal $=s\sqrt{2}$, so $s\sqrt{2}=10$, giving $s=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{2}}=5\sqrt{2}$.

sections.heading: Regular polygon interior and exterior angles

questions.q: Find the measure of each interior angle and each exterior angle of a regular octagon.
questions.answer: Sum of interior angles of an $n$-gon: $(n-2)180^\circ$. For $n=8$: $(6)(180^\circ)=1080^\circ$. Each interior angle: $\dfrac{1080^\circ}{8}=135^\circ$. Each exterior angle (supplementary to the interior angle): $180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$.

sections.heading: A multi-part composite figure and circle problem

questions.q: This question has three parts. A running track consists of a rectangle with two semicircular ends. The rectangle is 80 meters long and 40 meters wide, and the semicircles are attached to the two 40-meter-wide ends. (a) Find the radius of each semicircle. (b) Find the total perimeter (distance around) the track, in terms of $\pi$. (c) Find the total enclosed area of the track shape, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: (a) The semicircles are attached to the 40-meter ends, so the diameter of each semicircle is 40, giving radius $=20$. (b) Perimeter $=2(\text{rectangle length})+2(\text{semicircle arc length})$. The two semicircles together form one full circle's circumference: $2\pi(20)=40\pi$. Total perimeter: $2(80)+40\pi=160+40\pi$ meters. (c) Area $=\text{rectangle area}+\text{combined semicircle area}$. Rectangle area: $80\times40=3200$. The two semicircles together form one full circle: $\pi(20)^2=400\pi$. Total area: $3200+400\pi$ square meters.

A solid consists of a cylinder of radius 3 and height 3, topped with a hemisphere of the same radius. Find the total volume, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Cylinder volume: $\pi r^2h=\pi(9)(3)=27\pi$. Hemisphere volume: $\dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi(27)=18\pi$. Total volume: $27\pi+18\pi=45\pi$.
